title: In-dialog re-INVITE correlation under externally supplied SDP
objective: Turn historical ACE Direct JsSIP re-INVITE workarounds into a portable interoperability scenario that can detect stale SDP reuse, request-correlation overwrite, and signaling/media readiness divergence without copying the workaround forward.

historicalBasis.observation: ACE Direct pinned JsSIP 3.5.1 and replaced installed RTCSession/UA implementation files with local modifications. The modified RTCSession keeps re-INVITE request and SDP state outside the individual transaction and exposes respondReinvite() for application-controlled response handling.
historicalBasis.scope: Motivating interoperability evidence only. Baudot does not copy the patch forward and does not infer that current JsSIP, JAIN SIP, browsers, ACE Direct deployments, or other SIP implementations have the same defect.

assertions: one pending re-INVITE must not overwrite another pending request correlation
a successful re-INVITE response does not prove that the active media description is fresh or usable
stale SDP reuse must remain observable even when the SIP dialog stays established
late observations do not rewrite earlier evidence

proves: per-request correlation survives reversed response observation order
491 Request Pending remains bound to the later overlapping request identity
externally supplied SDP can be bound to one request by SHA-256
stale SDP reuse is detected even when signaling status is 200
doesNotProve: live overlapping SIP transactions on a networked dialog
media or RTT readiness after re-INVITE

proves: a live JAIN SIP UAS establishes an INVITE 200 ACK dialog with an independent UDP peer
a first in-dialog INVITE remains pending while a second independently injected INVITE arrives
the overlapping request receives 491 Request Pending on the wire
the earlier pending request later completes with 200 and its matching ACK
raw SIP requests and responses are preserved in the evidence manifest
doesNotProve: live stale or mismatched SDP handling
media or RTT readiness after re-INVITE

proves: a control re-INVITE returns fresh text/t140 SDP under 200 and reaches RTT ready
the control RTP bytes are independently parsed as the narrow Baudot RFC 4103 primary T140block primitive
a later re-INVITE can deliberately reuse the prior SDP answer while still returning 200
the stale answer is detected by SHA-256 against the intended fresh answer
the stale arm can preserve RTT negotiation while no first T.140 character reaches the intended fresh receiver
RTT readiness remains false when negotiation exists without a first T.140 character
doesNotProve: that ACE Direct or any contemporary implementation naturally emits stale SDP

runnableEvidence: message-level request correlation and externally supplied SDP binding
live overlapping in-dialog INVITE glare with 491 Request Pending
live control and stale-SDP RTT readiness arms
independent Python parsing of the received control T140block RTP packet
terminal scenario reduction joining transaction identity, SDP identity, and readiness evidence
requiredBeforeProven: repeatable execution evidence across more than one SIP implementation
standards-grounded reduction of any stack disagreement rather than treating implementation agreement as authority
broader re-INVITE timing and retry coverage beyond the single deterministic glare sequence
production-representative gateway or VRS endpoint observations without weakening the existing claim boundaries
terminal evidence bundle suitable for an explicit proven-state review

doesNotEstablish: root cause of any contemporary ACE Direct, browser, VRS, or WebRTC failure
that ACE Direct's historical workaround is incorrect
that module-level state necessarily caused a production defect
